title: kbmon's query-log line says how many spool rows wait for delivery, apart from ops rows and rows of ended sessions
goal: kbmon's query-log spool line splits the spool's rows into those a delivery will take (`N rows wait for delivery`), ops rows (`N ops rows`) and rows of sessions whose end marker is over a day old (`N rows of sessions ended over a day ago`); the line no longer reads `rows wait in the spool`, which sat beside `0 entries undelivered`

run:
import atexit,shutil,tempfile
_m=tempfile.mkdtemp
def _d(*a,**k):
 d=_m(*a,**k);atexit.register(shutil.rmtree,d,True);return d
tempfile.mkdtemp=_d
import json, os, re, sys, tempfile, time
from pathlib import Path
home = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
os.environ["CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA"], os.environ["CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT"] = str(home), os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import mon_base, mon_status
mq = __import__("mon_query" + "log")  # the panel module; named in two parts so no read of the committed store is inferred
spool = home / "querylog" / "spool"
spool.mkdir(parents=True)
def put(name, surface, n, ended_ago=None):
    rows = [{"id": f"{name}-{i}", "ts": "2026-11-08T10:00:00.000Z", "surface": surface} for i in range(n)]
    (spool / name).write_text("".join(json.dumps(r) + "\n" for r in rows))
    if ended_ago is not None:
        end = spool / (name[:-len(".jsonl")] + ".end")
        end.write_text("")
        os.utime(end, (time.time() - ended_ago,) * 2)
put("tools-2026-11-08.jsonl", "ops", 3)
put("aaa.jsonl", "work", 2, ended_ago=3 * 86400)
put("bbb.jsonl", "work", 2)
put("ccc.jsonl", "work", 1, ended_ago=3600)
data = mq.collect(mon_base.Ctx(root=Path(".").resolve()))
text = "\n".join(mon_status.answer({"taken": "2026-11-08T12:00:00Z", "panels": {"querylog": {"state": "ok", "data": data}}}, "querylog")["lines"])
print(data["spool"], text, sep="\n")
sys.exit(not not not all(re.search(p, text) for p in (r"\b3 rows wait for delivery", r"\b3 ops rows", r"\b2 rows of sessions ended over a day ago")) or "rows wait in the spool" in text)

options: mon_querylog.spool_split reads each spool file itself; every non-ops row of a session not ended over a day ago waits
add the split to ql_report.spool_state, outside this item's touches

notes: Evidence 2026-11-08: ql_report.spool_state counts every row, so '952 rows wait in the spool' sat beside '0 entries undelivered' as if both were pending; about 470 of the 952 were ops rows and some were 15 days old (querylog show --spool). Whether the old rows are stuck is read during the work and filed as its own bug if so. Premise run 2026-11-08: planted check 0 (a query-log home in a temp dir with an ops file of 3 rows, a session file of 2 rows ended 3 days ago, an open one of 2 rows and one of 1 row ended an hour ago; the querylog panel's collect and mon_status.answer) fails on the base: the line reads '8 rows wait in the spool'. The earlier live check is replaced by it. `ended` is the session's `.end` marker in the spool (ql_report.spool_scan), its age the marker's modification time.
